Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good evening and welcome to the Gallantt Ispat Limited's Q2 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should 
you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then 
zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Vanessa Fernandes from the Investor Relations team of 
Adfactors PR. Thank you, and over to you, Ms. Vanessa. 
Vanessa Fernandes: 
Thank you, Swapnali. Good evening, everyone. On behalf of Gallantt Ispat Limited, I would 
like to welcome you all to the earnings conference call for Q2 and H1 FY27. Today on the call, 
we have with us from the management Mr. Dindayal Jalan, Vice Chairman; Mr. Mayank 
Agarwal, Chief Executive Officer; and Mr. Amit Jalan, Chief Financial Officer of Gallantt Ispat 
Limited.  
 
We will begin the call with brief opening remarks from the management, followed by a Q&A 
session. All participant lines will be in listen-only mode during the management's remarks, and 
the floor will be open for questions thereafter.  
 
Please note that certain statements made during this call may be forward-looking in nature. Such 
forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results 
or projections to differ materially from those statements. Gallantt Ispat holds no responsibility 
for any actions taken based on such statements and undertakes no obligation to publicly update 
these forward-looking statements. 
 
I now hand over the call to Mr. Dindayal Jalan, Sir, for his opening remarks. Over to you, Sir. 
Dindayal Jalan:  
Thank you, Vanessa. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and a warm welcome to Gallantt 
Ispat's earnings conference call for the second quarter and first half of FY27. Let me begin with 
wider environment because it shaped this quarter in important ways. The global steel industry 
continues to operate in an uncertain setting. Geopolitical tensions, including the conflict in the 
Middle East, have kept energy, freight, and coal costs elevated. And trade flows have shifted as 
surplus from overseas looks to new buyers. 
 
India has not been fully insulated from this, but the domestic fundamentals remain strong, and 
our two home states, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, remain among the fastest-growing markets in 
the country. We see this as a long cycle, and we are building Gallantt to participate in it fully. 
Mayank will take you through the market trends in more detail. 
 
For Gallantt, Q2 was a quarter in which we chose to invest in our future capacity. We took a 
planned shutdown at our Gorakhpur plant to integrate the expanded capacity, and an unplanned 
extension of a power plant shutdown added to the impact. Mayank will take you through both 
in detail. 
 
 

 
Gallantt Ispat Limited 
 
 
October 21, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 12 
 
 
Revenue for the quarter was INR1,146 crores, 13% higher than a year ago, and in line with the 
previous quarter, as former realizations helped offset the effect of the shutdowns on our volumes. 
Our margins, however, were affected by the shutdowns and by higher input cost. It was all one-
time effect. They do not reflect any change in the underlying strength of our business. And as 
the new capacity comes on stream in Q3, we expect our performance to recover. 
 
Our strategy continues to rest on three anchors: integration, scale, and capital discipline. Each 
of these moved forward this quarter. On integration, Gallantt was awarded a coal block in 
Singrauli in August 2026, as disclosed to the exchanges. Together with our iron ore blocks in 
Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, this means Gallantt now holds both of the key raw materials for 
steel making. Over time, this will give us security of supply and a structurally lower cost base. 
This is the most durable advantage a steel company can build. 
 
On scale, our expansion from 1 to 1.23 million ton is now being integrated at Gorakhpur, and 
Mayank will take you through the through the progress. On capital discipline, we continue to 
carry no term loans for our projects, and our INR3,000 crores program remains funded through 
internal accruals. 
 
I would also like to address our medium-term growth plan. In our previous calls, we said that 
we'd share it with you this quarter. Since then, coal block award has changed the scale of what 
is possible for Gallantt. With both iron ore and coal now in our portfolio, we are evaluating a 
larger greenfield opportunity built around our raw material base rather than only extending our 
existing sites. 
 
A project of this nature depends on land acquisition and incentives from the state government, 
and we are working on that. We would rather come to you with a plan that is concrete and fully 
worked out, that's still taking shape. We therefore intend to present our growth plan in Quarter 
4 '27. 
 
What will not change is our focus on steel, our commitment to integrate, and our discipline on 
returns and on balance sheet. Gallantt has been built over two decades by staying focused and 
investing ahead of the opportunity. The steps we are taking this year in capacity, in raw material 
security, and in renewable energy are meant to position us for the next phase of India's growth. 
I am confident in the direction we have set. 
 
With that, I hand over to Mayank to take you through our operating performance. Over to you, 
Mayank. 
Mayank Agarwal:  
Thank you, Sir, and good afternoon, everyone. Let me begin with a brief word on the market. 
And then, as on our previous calls, take you through the quarter across our four pillars, that is 
volume growth, cost efficiency, an integration depth, margin expansions, and capital discipline. 
 
Domestic demand held up well through the first half. Finished steel consumption in India grew 
7.5% to about 85 million tons, ahead of growth in domestic production, even as the country 

 
Gallantt Ispat Limited 
 
 
October 21, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 12 
 
remained a net importer of finished steel. As the monsoon receded, prices across the value chain 
firmed up from August, and TMT prices in September were about 21% higher than a year ago. 
 
On the cost side, coal and freight stayed elevated. And prices of metallics, such as sponge iron 
and pig iron, rose sharply in the second half of the quarter. Demand is being driven by 
infrastructure, housing, and urbanization, and we expect activity in our market to pick up further 
as the construction season gets underway. 
 
The first pillar of volume growth. This quarter, our volumes were shaped by a deliberate decision 
at Gorakhpur as part of our expansion to 1.3 million tons annually. We are adding capacity at 
every stage of the chain at Gorakhpur, except sponge iron, including 22-megawatt of additional 
generation at our existing 78-megawatt captive power plant.  
 
Because Gorakhpur is a fully integrated plant from pellet through to TMT bars, new capacity 
cannot simply be added alongside running units. It has to be synchronized with them, and that 
requires a shutdown. We planned for this and used the same window to bring forward our 
maintenance of our existing units, so that we avoid a second interruption later in the year.  
 
Reflecting this, TMT sales for the quarter were 1,65,000 tons, compared with about 1,92,000 
tons in Q1 FY27. At Kutch, rolling mill utilization, which we identified as a focus area in the 
last quarter, was 68% in Quarter 2, compared with 66% in Quarter 1. The enhanced Gorakhpur 
capacity is expected to be operational in November '26. 
 
And with Gallantt Advance endorsed by Ajay Devgn and Janhvi Kapoor, and our dealer network 
in Uttar Pradesh, where we hold more than 25% of the submersible market, we have a ready 
channel to place the additional volumes. Alongside the input cost pressure, our costs were 
affected by an extended shutdown at our Gorakhpur power plant. 
 
What began as scheduled maintenance took longer than planned, as a turbine issue required 
specialist support. That work is now complete, and the plant is set to resume operations within 
a week. During this period, lower captive power availability raised our power cost, which is one 
of the main reasons margins were compressed this quarter. 
 
Our structural cost levers continue to build. Our 18-megawatt solar plant at Siddhpur in Gujarat 
is completed and set to resume operations by November 2026, and the 60-megawatt plant at 
Prayagraj, UP, which will serve to our Gorakhpur unit, remains on track for Q4 2027. Together, 
these are expected to save INR30 to INR40 crores annually in power cost. 
 
Upstream debottlenecking at our Gujarat unit remains on track for completion this financial year. 
And with the coal block that sir mentioned, alongside our iron blocks, our integration now 
extends to both key raw materials. At the iron ore blocks, exploration is progressing, and the 
environment and forest clearances processes are underway. And FY28 remained our target for 
them to become operational. 
Margins were compressed this quarter by the 2 shutdowns at Gorakhpur and by higher input 
costs, partly offset by better realization. Our CFO, Mr. Amit Jalan, will take you through the 
numbers. Looking ahead, the drivers of recovery are clear. In the near term, the expanded 

 
Gallantt Ispat Limited 
 
 
October 21, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 12 
 
Gorakhpur capacity, the restart of the power plant, and the firmer steel prices, as construction 
picks up after the monsoon, should all support the second half. 
Over the medium term, solar, the Gujarat debottlenecking, and captive mines, which we expect 
to add about INR2,000 per ton to EBITDA once operational, will lift our margins structurally. 
Our INR3,000 crores capex program continues to be funded entirely through internal accruals, 
and we carry no term loans for our projects. 
Capex in the first half was INR278 crores, as our projects at Gorakhpur and in renewable energy 
move towards completion. We remain watchful of input cost, but we enter the second half with 
a larger and more integrated asset base than before, and with the disruptions of this quarter 
largely behind us. 
With that, I hand over to Amit to take you through the financial highlights. 
Amit Jalan: 
Thank you, Sir. Good afternoon, everyone. Let me take you through our financial performance 
for the second quarter and the first half of FY27. Revenue from operation for the quarter was 
INR1,146 crores, an increase of 13% from INR1,013 crores in Q2 FY26, and in line with 
INR1,146 crores in the previous quarter. Other income for the quarter was INR18 crores. 
 
EBITDA for the quarter was INR111 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 9.64%, compared with 
the INR185 crores and 16.19% in Q1 FY27, and INR135 crores and 12.91% in Q2 FY26. 
EBITDA per ton was INR6,150, against INR8,010 in the previous quarter. The decline was 
driven by the planned and unplanned shutdowns at Gorakhpur and by higher input costs, partly 
offset by better realization. 
 
Employee costs were INR42 crores, against INR39 crores in Q1, and the finance cost was stable 
at INR9 crores. Profit before tax was INR83 crores, compared with the INR165 crores in Q1 
FY27, and INR103 crores in Q2 FY26. Profit after tax was INR61 crores, with the PAT margin 
of 5.3%, compared with INR124 crores and 10.8% in the previous quarter, and INR89 crores 
and 8.8% in the same quarter last year, earnings per share for the quarter is INR2.51. 
For the first half, revenue from operation grew 7% to INR2,292 crores, compared with INR2,141 
crores in H1 FY26. EBITDA was INR296 crores, with a margin of 12.91%, compared with 
INR382 crores and 17.85% a year earlier. Profit after tax was INR184 crores, compared with 
INR263 crores in H1 FY26, and earnings per share for the half year INR7.63 per share. 
Turning to the balance sheet. As of 30th September 2026, our net worth stood at INR3,487 
crores, up from INR3,316 crores in March. Borrowings were INR592 crores, mostly working 
capital facilities, and we continue to carry no term loan for our project. Against this, we held 
about INR426 crores in bank balances and liquid investments, along with INR266 crores in 
short-term treasury deployment, so we remains net cash positive. 
Inventory rose to INR669 crores from INR551 crores in the March. Capital work-in-progress 
increased to INR598 crores from INR349 crores in March, reflecting the project underway. 
Capex during the first half was INR278 crores, of which about INR141 crores was spent in 

 
Gallantt Ispat Limited 
 
 
October 21, 2026

quarter 2, all funded through internal accruals. Up to September 2026, we have spent INR650 
crores of the INR3,000 crores capex program. 
 
Shareholders approved a final dividend of INR2 per share for financial year 2026 at the AGM 
held on 30th September 2026. We expect our balance sheet to remain strong through FY27, with 
internal accruals as our primary source of funding for the current program. 
 
With that, I hand the call back to the moderator to open the floor for questions. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Sir. We will now begin with a question-and-answer session. We have the first 
question from the line of Vini Jain from Jain Investments. Please go ahead. 
Vini Jain: 
Hi. Congratulations on the Coal Block Award. So, my question to you is, could you explain what 
it means strategically now for Gallantt? You have both iron ore and coal resources. How does it

Mayank Agarwal: 
So, we have recently been allocated the coal blocks, and we are currently exploring and doing 
the due diligence to move forward with it. And iron ore blocks, as we mentioned, is under 
exploration. So, definitely, as I mentioned during my briefing, both these minerals are the key 
drivers for any steel industry. 
And once these blocks are operational in couple of years, the iron ore blocks are targeted for 
FY28, and definitely, once these 2 raw material are secured, it can be a very good next phase of 
growth for Gallantt. 
Vini Jain: 
Got it. I have one additional question to you. So, you now indicated the medium-term growth 
plan will be shared in about Q4 of FY27. How are you thinking about funding? Will internal 
accruals remain the primary source, or should we expect a mix of debt and equity in this? 
Dindayal Jalan: 
We are still working out, depending on what is the size of the project, what is the capacity, what 
are the opportunities. I think we will decide the capital restructuring. But I think as you have 
seen from our track record, we largely rely on internal accruals, and we rely less on the external 
borrowings. So, depending on the philosophy of the group and the requirement of the project, 
we'll decide the mix of the funding. 
Vini Jain: 
Makes sense. Got it. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. We have the next question from the line of Preeti Sharma from Invest First Advisors. 
Please go ahead. 
Preeti Sharma: 
Thank you. Sir, firstly, congratulations on a good set of numbers. I had a couple of questions, so 
I'll say them one by one. So, my question is, since the TMT prices have risen sharply since 
August, how sustainable do you think this is as we move into the construction season? And what 
are you seeing in your markets in October? 
Mayank Agarwal: 
Okay. So, yes, steel prices, as we mentioned, has significantly risen. And what is exciting is that 
this price increase comes at a time where the lean period, the monsoon period was ongoing, and 
it is broadly based on the domestic demand cycle. 

 
Gallantt Ispat Limited

So, once the monsoon is now over, and we enter the enter the month of November, where the 
construction activities pick up, and they peak in December onwards, we feel that the prices 
would remain strong in future, leading to good margins. Some bit of it is obviously being passed 
on to the energy prices due to geopolitical situations, but largely it is exciting, and it would add 
a bit to EBITDA going forward. 
Preeti Sharma: 
Okay, noted. Sir, my second question would be on the margin. Since margins were under 
pressure this quarter, how much of the decline would you attribute to the one-time shutdown 
versus the input costs? And what level of margins should we expect on these as these normalize 
in the second half? 
Mayank Agarwal: 
So, there are a couple of factors, actually besides the shutdown, while one bit of it was shutdown, 
the second bit of it is that the price increase has happened only in the last one month, in 
September. So, ideally, the effect of the risen prices will come into Q3. So, in Q2, while the coal 
prices increased, the realization increased much later, not making any impact in Q2 broadly, 
majorly. 
And the shutdowns, both had effect. So, if we talk about the coal pricing, the coal prices has 
affected to the tune of about  4.5% to 5% on the raw material cost, on the total sales revenue. 
That is the impact of the coal prices. So, if we say 5%, it's around INR2,500 per ton on the TMT 
prices. 
And there has been a 1% price increase on the iron ore front also. So, all put together, it's about 
INR3,000 a ton of price increase that we have seen in Q2 in the raw material side, whereas the 
prices of the finished product have increased by 20%. So, if the prices continue to remain strong, 
as we expect, then definitely it will result into much better EBITDAs. 
Preeti Sharma: 
Okay. Got it. Sir, my last question is, so basically on the captive iron ore mines, is that INR2,000 
per ton EBITDA benefit still the right number, or how will it phase once the production starts in 
FY28? 
Mayank Agarwal: 
Yes. So, INR2,000 is what we are expecting would be added with the iron ore mines on the 
EBITDA of the steel prices. And FY28 is what we plan to make it operational. And definitely, 
in the first 1 or 2 years, it would probably not make, I mean, it would not be completely feeding 
the steel plants to the tune of 100% from iron ore mines. But as and how, in a year or 2 post-
FY28, the mining activity increases and the capacities are utilized at the mines, it would add that 
much to the EBITDA. 
Preeti Sharma: 
Okay, noted. Thank you so much and all the best, sir. 
Mayank Agarwal: 
Thank you.

Thank you. We have the next question from the line of Anirudh Sharma from Ekaant 
Investments. Please go ahead.

side. So, firstly, I wanted to know that India remained a net importer of finished steel in the first

Mayank Agarwal: 
So, India, yes, remained a net importer, but construction activity, as we mentioned, has
